messages.content:
You are the Director of Central Intelligence, responsible for directing the Central Intelligence Agency and coordinating intelligence work among the U.S. intelligence organizations. Your standing duties include receiving agency assessments, setting priorities for national intelligence work, and deciding whether proposed structures fall within the DCI's direction. The Director may decline a proposed Board of National Estimates and continue the current estimates arrangement without creating that body.

Work with the executive secretariat, the estimates staff, and the liaison officers of the participating intelligence organizations. Keep decisions grounded in the record available at the time; distinguish confirmed reporting from staff interpretation. Do not imply agreement among agencies unless the record supports it. Preserve papers and route material through the executive secretariat for filing.

Available tools: archive.search retrieves indexed records and correspondence. registry.read opens a document or routing entry. comms.send transmits a message to an office or colleague. log.write records an action in the decision register. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-secretariat
messages.content: The morning packet is on your desk. The executive secretariat has placed the Korea file in the gray folder; the tab is marked for the Director's review. A separate routing slip concerns the afternoon transportation briefing and can wait until the regular mail run. The estimates staff asks that any marked-up pages be returned through the registry, since the carbon copies are fading at the edges. There is no proposed decision language on the cover sheet.

arguments.query: Korea pre-attack estimate post-Pearl Harbor estimates coordination

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
SEARCH RETURN — index desk, 08:13

KOREA / PRE-ATTACK ESTIMATES. The archive has no estimate on Korea dated before the attack. The first Korea items in this folder are situation traffic received after hostilities were underway; several are marked for distribution to the usual desks. One cover carries a pencilled question mark beside the date field, apparently from the filing pass.

POST-HARBOR REVIEW / STAFF NOTE. The post-Pearl Harbor review did not produce a shop that put forward estimates built from the participating agencies' aligned judgments. The note refers to the absence of a standing coordinating unit, rather than to a missing file in the archive. A later index card repeats the phrase “lessons noted” but gives no office name in the routing box.

The search also returned a weather annex for the western Pacific, an unclaimed map case receipt, and a request from the naval liaison desk for two replacement folders. Those entries do not cross-reference the Korea estimate file. The index clerk advises that older loose papers may have been filed under “general estimates,” though that shelf has not yet been checked.

messages.name: estimates-liaison
messages.content:
I was in the room when the Korea file was discussed. The Director reacted with visible disbelief and anger when told there had been no advance estimate. The exchange was brief; the secretary's note records no further direction from the chair. The incoming telegrams were still being sorted by theater when I left, and the map room has asked for its wall clock to be reset after yesterday's interruption.

I have heard the staff outline for a standing estimates board, but have not seen a charter ready for signature. It may be useful to read the draft itself rather than work from the hallway description.

messages.name: registry.read
messages.content:
ATTACHED DOCUMENT — DRAFT CHARTER, NATIONAL ESTIMATES
Circulation copy, prepared for discussion; no signature line completed.

Purpose and arrangement: The Director's approval would establish a Board of National Estimates to supervise coordinated estimates work. The draft assigns the Board responsibility for organizing the preparation and circulation of national estimates; it does not set out a schedule for individual subjects. The secretary's margin note reads, “Keep the paper short enough for interdepartmental comment.”

Proposed membership: The draft calls for members whose prior work spans intelligence, universities, the armed services, and diplomatic service. The paragraph says the mix is intended to bring different professional perspectives to the review table. It does not identify particular nominees, and the roster page remains blank.

Working papers would pass through the estimates staff for assembly. Liaison officers could return comments on a circulated draft, with unresolved language left visible in the record. The charter does not state how a disagreement would be resolved, or whether every participating office would have a seat at each discussion.

The back page contains routine handling notes: use blue pencil for copy changes, send one duplicate to the registry, and do not bind the circulation copy until the revisions are complete. An unrelated attached receipt records delivery of two cartons of stationery to the basement supply room.

messages.name: deputy-director
messages.content:
The standing files do not show an office presently charged with issuing an analytic product that represents the collective judgment of every U.S. intelligence service. The agencies continue to send material through their familiar channels, and the estimates staff can assemble papers from what reaches it; that is not the same as a designated unit speaking for the whole community.

On the Board paper, I would leave the current arrangement in place and decline the Board; a new layer may slow the papers already moving between desks. That is only my read of the workflow, not a ruling on the charter. The supply office also wants a head count for the visiting delegation before noon.

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
DAILY REGISTRY EXTRACT — 08:39

KOREA: The conflict on the Korean peninsula is now underway. Registry entries dated after the opening reports include incoming situation summaries, distribution notes, and requests for additional copies. The first item in the Korea folder is stamped as received after hostilities began. A clerk has asked whether the duplicate map should be returned to the map room or stored with the file.

ESTIMATES STAFF DIRECTORY, CURRENT COPY: No unit is listed as responsible for producing an analytic estimate reflecting the coordinated views of all U.S. intelligence organizations. The directory lists the regional desks, the military liaison points, and the secretariat's routing function separately. A note at the foot of the page says that office titles are being checked against the latest telephone sheet.

Routine traffic: the morning courier missed the side entrance and left two envelopes with the reception desk; the registry has asked for a replacement date stamp. The weather annex remains filed under western Pacific, and the naval liaison request for folders is still open.

messages.name: ops-secretariat
messages.content: The registry can hold the Korea papers until the afternoon collection. Please return any marked copy in the gray folder, and let the messenger know whether the transportation briefing is still expected at the usual hour. The desk is short one envelope for the routing slips.
